ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

On the basis of this shape-selective feature , highly effective molecular separations and selective catalytic conversions can be achieved within zeolitic structures that are difficult to accomplish with other materials and/or techniques . $ ^ { 1-3 } $ So far, several shape-selectivity mechanisms have been elucidated and applications identified. $ ^{2-18} $ In common molecular sieving, bulky molecules adsorb preferentially over bulkier species as a result of steric constraints imposed by the zeolites' framework, e.g., linear alkane molecules compared to branched isomers. $ ^{19-23} $ Besides this common adsorption competition based on molecular bulkiness, the reverse phenomenon can also occur, i.e., competitive adsorption in favor of the bulkier species. The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. Since both adsorbed molecules are constrained in the zeolite cavity their entropy contributions in the adsorption complexes were corrected as follows: the translational and rotational degrees of freedom were reduced by 1 and 1.28 [37]. The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

descriptor_candidates.name: conf_free_volume_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Molecular-to-pore size mismatch governs entropy loss: the descriptor log(Vol/(AV*10^6/(LabuteASA+1))) correlates with the fraction of gas-phase entropy retained upon adsorption; adding this nonlinear transform on top of the 14-input network reduces MAE of s_ads/s_gas by at least 10% versus the baseline network.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference (not directly stated in evidence): entropy loss arises from translational/rotational constraint when molecular volume (Vol) fills the occupiable pore volume (AV). Tight confinement (large Vol relative to AV) restricts more degrees of freedom (E01, E03). LabuteASA rescales the accessible free space per unit surface, capturing effective free volume rather than total volume.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If including this descriptor in the 14-input network does not improve MAE of entropy loss/R on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs (or degrades it), the size-mismatch mechanism as encoded here is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_asymmetry_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Beyond volumetric filling, molecular shape anisotropy modulates entropy loss: elongated/asymmetric molecules (high PMI2/PMI1, high PBF/SPAN) lose more rotational entropy in channel-type pores than compact ones at equal Vol/AV; multiplying this shape term into the network reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 5% versus the baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E01 notes the role of 'molecular shape and confinement in nanoporous structures ... remains to be determined', and E05 shows shape-selectivity strongly alters adsorption states of near-identical molecules. PMI ratios encode rod-like vs. spherical geometry; PBF/SPAN encodes the fraction of the molecular span touching the pore wall. Anisotropic molecules cannot freely rotate in cylindrical pores, so rotational entropy loss is shape-dependent.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If residuals of the baseline model show no significant correlation (|r| < 0.2) with (PMI2/PMI1)*(PBF/SPAN)^2, or adding the descriptor yields no MAE improvement, the shape-asymmetry mechanism is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_aperture_fraction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the tightness of pore apertures relative to molecular mass: the term lsd_p - lsd_f (pore-limiting vs. largest free diameter difference) times density and ASA per unit MW encodes how severely the narrowest constriction clips translational freedom; including it reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 8% versus baseline, especially for small-pore frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E01 shows frameworks with narrow channels (TON) cause the largest entropy loss versus large-cage FAU; E07 notes type-I isotherms of micropores (constriction-dominated adsorption). lsd_p - lsd_f measures the gap between limiting aperture and largest cavity, so frameworks dominated by constrictions (small gap) should impose stronger translational constraints. ASA*density/MW expresses accessible surface contacted per molecular mass.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the aperture-gap descriptor shows no significant correlation with entropy loss residuals for small-pore (lsd_p < ~0.65 nm, cf. E04) subsets, or no MAE improvement overall, the constriction-control hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_curvature_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases when accessible surface area is packed into narrow, low-diameter channels: the ratio LabuteASA*lsd_f/(Vol*(lsd_p+1)) is high for frameworks with large contacted surface but small limiting apertures relative to molecular volume, implying greater clipping of translational/rotational freedom. Adding this descriptor to the 14-input network reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 5% versus the retained baseline (MAE_R = 0.5581).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference (not directly stated in evidence): E01 shows adsorbed entropy never exceeds gas-phase entropy and that entropy loss is framework-specific (TON largest, FAU smallest); E03 shows occupiable volume alone captures much of the loss. The residual, unexplained part likely reflects surface-contact geometry: a molecule touching more wall area per unit of free volume in a narrow channel loses more configurational entropy. LabuteASA/Vol is a surface-to-volume ratio; multiplying by lsd_f/(lsd_p+1) down-weights frameworks with wide cavities beyond the constriction, where wall contact is more transient.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's correlation with baseline-model residuals is |r| < 0.2, or adding it to the network does not improve held-out MAE of entropy loss/R relative to the round-2 retained model, the surface-contact mechanism as encoded is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: aniso_pore_window_penalty
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss is governed by the match between molecular principal-axis asymmetry and the aperture-to-cavity ratio: elongated molecules (high sqrt(PMI3/PMI1)) retain more entropy in frameworks where lsd_p is large relative to lsd_f (cage-like, room to reorient), but lose more in constricted channels. Including this interaction descriptor reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 5% versus baseline, with the largest gains for anisotropic adsorbates in channel frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E05 shows shape-selective steric matching produces distinct adsorption states for near-identical molecules; E09 (Fig. 19) shows molecular symmetry strongly alters rotational/translational dynamics under confinement; E01 states the shape-confinement entropy relation 'remains to be determined'. The product encodes an interaction: molecular anisotropy matters most when the pore is channel-like (small lsd_p/lsd_f), because reorientation is blocked by walls at the constriction.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If residuals of the baseline model show no significant correlation with the descriptor within the elongated-molecule subset (e.g., PMI3/PMI1 above the dataset median), or overall MAE does not improve, the anisotropy-cavity interaction mechanism is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_density_gravity
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with framework packing density (low AV at high framework density leaves little free space per mass) combined with molecular inertia per size (Vol per unit mass): heavy, compact molecules in densely packed frameworks are most strongly vibrationally caged. Adding this descriptor reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 5% versus the round-2 retained model, especially for frameworks with low AV (tight micropores).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E07 notes type-I isotherms characterize narrow micropores where adsorption is constriction-dominated; E03 establishes occupiable volume as the primary single descriptor, so residuals should carry information about how densely the framework packs solid mass around that volume. exp(-AV*density) is large only when free volume per framework mass is small; Vol/(MW+20) contrasts compact-heavy molecules (caged, vibrational entropy suppressed) against light or voluminous ones. Density is used on its native numerical scale only as a monotonic packing index, without assigning physical units.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor shows no significant correlation with baseline residuals on the low-AV (below-median) subset, or yields no MAE improvement on held-out pairs, the packing-cage mechanism as encoded is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: aperture_to_volume_tortuosity
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed jointly by aperture-to-cavity ratio and specific surface exposure: molecules in frameworks where the limiting aperture is small relative to the largest free dimension (low lsd_p/lsd_f) but which expose high surface area per pore volume (ASA per AV) lose more entropy, because they repeatedly contact constricted walls along the diffusion path. Adding this descriptor to the retained 14-input network (baseline MAE_R = 0.5483) reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 3% on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference (not directly stated in evidence): E01 shows entropy loss is framework-specific (TON worst, FAU mildest), suggesting path tortuosity and constriction frequency matter beyond occupiable volume alone (E03). ASA/AV approximates wall contact per unit free space; lsd_p/(lsd_f+1) penalizes constriction-dominated channel systems; PBF rescales by the fraction of molecular span near walls. The product encodes a 'how much wall contact per constriction traversed' mechanism.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If residuals of the retained baseline model show |r| < 0.2 with this descriptor, or held-out MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve relative to MAE_R = 0.5483, the constriction-contact-frequency mechanism as encoded is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: geometric_elongation_caging
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss depends on the mismatch between molecular span and pore geometric diameter in densely packed frameworks: long, extended molecules (high SPAN relative to GeDi) housed in frameworks with little free volume per mass (high AV*density product, low exp term) cannot reorient and lose disproportionately more rotational entropy than compact molecules in spacious frameworks. Including this interaction descriptor reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 3% versus the retained baseline, with the largest gains for elongated adsorbates (SPAN/GeDi above dataset median) in low-AV frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E05 shows steric shape matching creates distinct adsorption states for near-identical molecules; E09 (Fig. 19) shows molecular symmetry strongly alters rotational/translational dynamics under confinement; E08 shows framework flexibility governs uptake of bulky molecules, implying that tight packing leaves little room for reorientation. SPAN/GeDi contrasts longest dimension with geometric diameter (anisotropy index); exp(-AV*density) is a monotonic packing index on the source numerical scale (no physical units assigned).
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If within the elongated-molecule subset (SPAN/GeDi above median) the descriptor's correlation with baseline residuals is |r| < 0.2, or overall held-out MAE does not improve, the shape-packing caging mechanism as encoded is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: inertia_volume_vibrational_load
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: A previously unexplained residual of entropy loss reflects vibrational entropy suppression: massive, compact molecules (high MW, low PMI1 per unit Vol) sitting in frameworks with low free volume per mass (low AV*density) are vibrationally caged, converting otherwise-translational freedom into stiff frustrated modes. Because all prior descriptors captured translational/rotational loss, adding this mass-inertia-versus-packing descriptor reduces MAE of entropy loss/R by at least 3% versus the retained baseline, especially for heavy adsorbates (MW above median) in tight micropores.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E06 notes adsorbed molecules retain vibrational entropy contributions while translational/rotational modes are reduced under confinement; E01 derives translational entropy loss via the Sackur–Tetrode equation (mass dependence), implying mass-weighted terms may still carry residual signal once shape/volume effects are absorbed by the network. Vol/PMI1 contrasts compact-heavy vs. diffuse-light molecules; AV*density acts as a monotonic framework-packing index on the native numerical scale.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor shows no significant correlation (|r| < 0.2) with baseline residuals in the heavy-adsorbate (MW above median) and low-AV subsets, or no held-out MAE improvement relative to MAE_R = 0.5483, the vibrational-caging mass mechanism as encoded is falsified.
